'''Kurma''' is a sweet fried dough coated in a sugar syrup.

==Ingredients==
===Kurma dough===
*2 cloves [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], finely grated
*1 tin (1 ⅔ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) [[Cookbook:Evaporated milk|evaporated milk]]
*⅔ tin (1 ¼ cups) [[Cookbook:Condensed milk|sweetened condensed milk]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Coconut Cream|coconut cream]]
*6 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] powder
*1 stick (½ cup) [[Cookbook:butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:margarine|margarine]]
*6 dashes Angostura bitters

===Sugar syrup===
*2 cups [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]

==Procedure==
===Kurma dough===
#Mix flour, ginger, cinnamon, and butter in a large bowl.
#Mix evaporated milk, coconut cream, condensed milk, and Angostura bitters in a separate bowl.
#Pour the liquid mixture into the mixture of dry ingredients a little bit at a time. Mix until a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] forms. The dough should be "tough;" that is, not stretchy.
#Divide the dough into two balls. This makes it more manageable. Roll each ball out until about 1 cm thick.
#Cut dough into strips.
#Heat ½ cup of oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
#[[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] batches of the kurma dough in the oil, turning often.
#Remove when golden brown on all sides.

===Sugar syrup===
#Heat sugar and water over medium heat.
#Stir so that sugar is completely wet.
#When the sugar is dissolved and the mixture is clear, remove from heat.
#Pour over kurma, and stir quickly to coat evenly.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Short, thin strips of dough work best. Fat, long pieces tend to fall apart and be soft inside.
*If kurma is browning quickly and unevenly, turn heat down.
